The estimand is beta, the average effect of random assignment to the Pathways to Work program (intention-to-treat, assignment rather than participation) on monthly earnings at 12 months, conditional on site and the baseline covariates. Treatment was randomized within site (about half per site), so assignment is treated as independent of potential outcomes given site. Observations (participants) are assumed independent. Errors are not assumed normal, and their variances are not assumed equal: error variance may differ across participants (heteroskedasticity allowed), and no population variance is treated as known. No other population parameters are fixed at known values.
commit_null: H0: beta = 0, i.e. the treatment coefficient (the program's effect on 12-month monthly earnings, adjusting for site and baseline covariates) is zero. The alternative is two-sided (beta ≠ 0).
commit_population: Adults seeking work or better jobs who enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four sites and were randomly assigned within site to the program or to a control group with access to existing public services.
commit_outcome: earnings_m12: earnings in dollars for the month before the 12-month follow-up, with 0 for participants not employed. Used in levels, untransformed.
commit_sample_restrictions: none. The full sample of all randomized participants was used, with no subgroup, filter, or exclusion. The codebook reports complete data, so no complete-case restriction applied.

commit_model: Linear regression model for participants in the randomized Pathways to Work trial: training_m12_i = alpha + beta*treatment_i + gamma_2*1[site_i=2] + gamma_3*1[site_i=3] + gamma_4*1[site_i=4] + e_i, with E[e_i | treatment_i, site_i] = 0. Treatment was randomly assigned within site (blocked randomization), so beta is interpreted as the site-adjusted average causal effect of assignment to the program (intent-to-treat) on the outcome. Site indicators (sites 1–4, site 1 as reference) are the only conditioning variables; no baseline covariates are included. Observations (participants) are treated as independent. Errors may be heteroskedastic: no distributional form (e.g., normality) is assumed for the outcome or errors, and no restriction on or known value of the error variances is imposed. No population parameters are treated as known or fixed.
commit_null: H0: beta = 0, i.e., the coefficient on treatment (the site-adjusted effect of program assignment on 12-month training enrollment among parents) is zero; two-sided alternative beta ≠ 0.
commit_population: Adults enrolled in the four-site Pathways to Work randomized evaluation who, at random assignment, lived with at least one child under 18 (parents).
commit_outcome: training_m12: binary indicator (1/0) of being enrolled in education or job training in the survey week at the 12-month follow-up, used untransformed (linear probability model; the effect is a difference in proportions).
commit_sample_restrictions: Analyst-imposed subgroup restriction to participants with parent == 1 (selected after an exploratory search across outcomes, follow-ups, and subgroups). No other filters; no complete-case restriction was needed since the codebook states all variables are observed for all participants.

commit_model: Linear regression model for participants in a within-site randomized trial: fin_security_m6 = b0 + b1*treatment + b2*parent + b3*(treatment x parent) + site indicators (sites 2-4) + site indicators x parent + b_age*age + b_f*female + education indicators (levels 2,3,4 vs 1) + b_hh*household_size + b_e*employed_baseline + b_eb*earnings_baseline + b_mu*months_unemployed_baseline + error. Restriction: E[error | regressors] = 0 (linear conditional mean with additive, common covariate slopes across parent groups and treatment arms; site intercepts allowed to differ by parent status). No distributional form is assumed for the error, and no homoskedasticity: error variance may differ arbitrarily across observations, with no known or fixed variance. Observations (participants) are treated as independent; randomization of treatment within site provides identification. Estimand: b3, the difference in the covariate-adjusted average treatment effect of assignment to Pathways to Work on the 6-month financial security index between parents and non-parents (parent effect minus non-parent effect). No population parameters are treated as known or fixed.
commit_null: H0: b3 = 0, i.e. the coefficient on treatment x parent is zero (the program's effect on 6-month financial security is the same for parents and non-parents), tested two-sided against b3 ≠ 0.
commit_population: Adults seeking work or better jobs who enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at the four study sites, randomized within site to the program or to control.
commit_outcome: fin_security_m6: the financial security index (0-20, higher means more secure) measured 6 months after random assignment, used untransformed in its original units.
commit_sample_restrictions: None. All 2,000 supplied participants were used, with no subgroup, filter or complete-case restriction. Parent status (lives with a child under 18) enters only as a moderator in the interaction and is not a sample restriction.

commit_model: Linear regression (linear probability model) of the binary 12-month employment indicator on the random-assignment indicator plus additive site fixed effects: E[employed_m12 | treatment, site] = alpha + beta*treatment + sum_{s=2..4} gamma_s*1(site = s). Site indicators are included as intrinsic conditioning variables because randomization was conducted within site; no other baseline covariates are included in the selected model. Estimand is beta, the intention-to-treat effect of assignment to Pathways to Work on the probability of being employed in the 12-month survey week, conditional on site (a site-fixed-effects-weighted combination of within-site assignment effects). No distributional family is assumed for the errors beyond the conditional-mean specification; error variances may differ across observations (heteroskedasticity allowed, no homoskedasticity or equal-variance restriction), and no population variance is treated as known. Observations (participants) are assumed independent of one another; no clustering or other within-group dependence is modeled. No population parameters are fixed at known values.
commit_null: H0: beta = 0, i.e., the coefficient on treatment (the site-conditional intention-to-treat effect of program assignment on the 12-month employment probability) equals zero, tested two-sided against beta ≠ 0; the intercept and site coefficients are unrestricted.
commit_population: Adults seeking work or better jobs who enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four sites and were randomly assigned within site to the program or to a control group with access to existing public services.
commit_outcome: employed_m12: indicator equal to 1 if the participant was employed in the survey week at the 12-month follow-up after random assignment, 0 otherwise; used untransformed on its 0/1 scale.
commit_sample_restrictions: No subgroup, eligibility, or outcome filter was imposed; the full sample of all participants across all four sites and both arms is used. The only analyst-imposed rule is a complete-case restriction on the three analysis variables (site, treatment, employed_m12), applied in score.py; in the supplied data every variable is observed for every participant, so this rule removes no rows.

commit_model: Linear regression model (conditional mean specification) for participants in the Pathways to Work randomized trial, among those under age 30 at random assignment: E[Y | treatment, site, X] = alpha + beta*treatment + site fixed effects (indicators for sites 2–4, site 1 as reference) + gamma'X. X are the baseline covariates: age (linear), female, parent, education category indicators (levels 2, 3, 4 vs. 1), household_size, employed_baseline, earnings_baseline, months_unemployed_baseline. The estimand beta is the site- and covariate-adjusted average effect of assignment to the program (intention-to-treat), versus assignment to control, on the outcome. Treatment was randomly assigned within site, so site is included as an intrinsic conditioning variable. Observations (participants) are assumed independent. Error variances may differ across observations (heteroskedasticity allowed); no distributional form for the errors is assumed and no population variance is treated as known. No other population parameters are fixed.
commit_null: H0: beta = 0, i.e. the coefficient on treatment (the adjusted intention-to-treat effect on the employment share) is zero. Two-sided alternative: beta ≠ 0.
commit_population: Adults enrolled in the four-site Pathways to Work randomized evaluation who were under 30 years old at random assignment.
commit_outcome: Share of the two follow-up surveys at which the participant was employed: (employed_m6 + employed_m12) / 2. Takes values 0, 0.5 or 1, where employed_m6 and employed_m12 are the binary survey-week employment indicators at 6 and 12 months after random assignment.
commit_sample_restrictions: Analyst-imposed subgroup restriction to participants with age < 30 at random assignment. I chose this cutoff after exploring the data. No other filters, and no complete-case restriction: the codebook says all variables are observed for all participants. Design eligibility (adults enrolled and randomized within the four sites) is unchanged.

commit_model: Linear regression model for each participant's 12-month earnings: E[earnings_m12 | treatment, site, X] = alpha + tau*treatment + site fixed effects (indicators for sites 2–4, with site 1 as reference) + linear terms in age, female, parent, household_size, employed_baseline, earnings_baseline and months_unemployed_baseline, plus indicators for education categories 2–4 (category 1 as reference). The estimand is tau: the effect of random assignment to Pathways to Work (intention-to-treat), versus assignment to control, on mean monthly earnings at 12 months, holding site and baseline covariates fixed. Under the within-site randomization this is the site-adjusted average effect of assignment. Site indicators are intrinsic controls because randomization was done within site. Baseline covariates are added as conditioning variables. Observations (participants) are assumed independent. Error variances may differ across participants (heteroskedasticity allowed). No distributional form (e.g., normality) is assumed for earnings or the errors, and no population variance is treated as known or restricted. The design's treatment-assignment probability within each site is one half.
commit_null: H0: tau = 0, meaning the coefficient on treatment is zero and assignment to the program has no effect on mean 12-month monthly earnings once site and baseline covariates are held fixed. The alternative is two-sided: tau ≠ 0.
commit_population: Adults seeking work or better jobs who enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four sites and were randomly assigned, within site, to the program or to control.
commit_outcome: earnings_m12: earnings in the month before the 12-month follow-up, in dollars, set to 0 if not employed. It is used untransformed, in levels, not as a change score or index.
commit_sample_restrictions: none. The full sample of all participants was used, with no subgroup, filter or complete-case restriction imposed by the analyst. The codebook says all variables are observed for every participant.

commit_model: Linear regression model for each participant i: earnings_m12_i = alpha + tau*treatment_i + site fixed effects (indicators for sites 2–4, site 1 as reference) + beta1*age + beta2*female + beta3*parent + education indicators (categories 2, 3, 4 vs. 1 as reference) + beta4*household_size + beta5*employed_baseline + beta6*earnings_baseline + beta7*months_unemployed_baseline + e_i. The model is linear and additive in these terms. Age, household size, baseline earnings and months unemployed enter linearly. Education enters as a categorical factor and site as fixed effects. The treatment effect tau is a single constant, with no treatment-by-covariate or treatment-by-site interactions. Errors are mean-zero conditional on the regressors. They are assumed independent across participants, but their variances may differ across participants (heteroskedasticity allowed). No particular error distribution (for example normality) is assumed, and no population variance is treated as known or restricted. Treatment was randomly assigned within site (about half to the program), so tau is interpreted as the intent-to-treat effect of being assigned to Pathways to Work on monthly earnings at 12 months, conditional on site and the baseline covariates. No other population parameters are fixed at specified values.
commit_null: H0: tau = 0. The coefficient on treatment (the intent-to-treat effect of program assignment on earnings at 12 months, conditional on site and the baseline covariates) is zero. The alternative is two-sided: tau ≠ 0.
commit_population: Adults seeking work or better jobs who enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at the four evaluation sites and were randomly assigned within site to the program or the control group (which could use existing public services).
commit_outcome: earnings_m12: earnings in the month before the 12-month follow-up, in dollars, with 0 for those not employed. Used untransformed, on the raw dollar scale, with no winsorizing, logging or standardizing.
commit_sample_restrictions: none. I imposed no additional restriction: the analysis uses all randomized participants in the supplied data, with no subgroup or filter. Per the codebook, every variable is observed for everyone, so no complete-case restriction was needed.

commit_model: Linear regression model for participants in a within-site (stratified) randomized trial: earnings_m12_i = alpha + tau*treatment_i + sum_{s=2..4} gamma_s*1[site_i = s] + beta'X_i + e_i, where treatment is the randomly assigned program indicator (1 = program, 0 = control), site fixed effects are included because randomization was conducted within site, and X_i are baseline covariates: age, female, parent, education entered as categorical indicators (levels 2, 3, 4 vs. 1), household_size, employed_baseline, earnings_baseline, months_unemployed_baseline. The estimand tau is the average effect of assignment to the program (intent-to-treat) on 12-month monthly earnings, conditional on site and the baseline covariates. Errors are assumed mean zero conditional on the regressors and independent across participants; no distributional form (e.g., normality) is imposed on the errors, and error variances are allowed to differ across participants (heteroskedasticity permitted, no homoskedasticity restriction). No population parameters are treated as known or fixed.
commit_null: H0: tau = 0, i.e., the coefficient on treatment (effect of program assignment on 12-month earnings, adjusting for site and baseline covariates) equals zero, tested against the two-sided alternative tau != 0.
commit_population: Adults seeking work or better jobs who enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at the four evaluation sites (all randomized participants, full sample).
commit_outcome: earnings_m12: earnings in the previous month, in dollars (0 if not employed), measured 12 months after random assignment; untransformed (levels, no logs, winsorizing, or trimming).
commit_sample_restrictions: none

commit_model: Linear model for one participant's outcome: earnings_m12 = alpha + tau*treatment + site fixed effects (indicators for sites 2, 3, 4, with site 1 as reference) + error. The error has conditional mean zero given treatment and site. Treatment was randomly assigned within site, about half to the program and half to control. The estimand tau is the intent-to-treat effect of assignment to Pathways to Work on 12-month earnings, i.e. the treatment-control difference in mean earnings_m12, conditional on site and pooled across the four sites with the regression's implied weights. Observations are independent across participants. Error variances may differ across participants (heteroskedasticity allowed). No distributional form such as normality is assumed for the outcome or the errors. No population variance or other parameter is treated as known or fixed. No baseline covariates beyond the site indicators are in the model.
commit_null: H0: tau = 0. The coefficient on treatment (the site-adjusted intent-to-treat effect of program assignment on 12-month earnings) is zero. The alternative is two-sided: tau ≠ 0.
commit_population: Adults enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four sites, randomly assigned within site to the program or to a control group that could use existing public services.
commit_outcome: earnings_m12: earnings in the month before the 12-month follow-up survey, in dollars (0 if not employed). It is used untransformed, in levels, with no logging, winsorizing or standardization.
commit_sample_restrictions: none

commit_model: A linear regression model for the parent subgroup: E[hardship_i | treatment_i, site_i] = alpha + beta*treatment_i + sum over sites 2-4 of gamma_s*1{site_i = s}. Site indicators (site 1 is the reference) are the built-in conditioning variables, because randomization happened within site. No baseline covariates are included. The estimand is beta: the treatment-control difference in mean hardship count among parents, adjusted for site and identified by random assignment within site. Observations are treated as independent across participants. No distributional form is assumed for the outcome. Error variances are not assumed to be equal: heteroskedasticity across observations is allowed. No population parameters, such as variances, are treated as known or fixed.
commit_null: H0: beta = 0. That is, the coefficient on treatment is zero, meaning no site-adjusted difference in mean hardship count between program and control parents. The alternative is two-sided (beta ≠ 0).
commit_population: Adults enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at the four sites who were living with at least one child under 18 at random assignment (parents).
commit_outcome: Material-hardship count, ranging from 0 to 4: the unweighted sum of four binary indicators, food_insecure_m6 + debt_collections_m6 + food_insecure_m12 + debt_collections_m12. These are household food insecurity in the past 30 days and having a debt in collections in the past 6 months, each measured at the 6-month and 12-month follow-ups.
commit_sample_restrictions: The only restriction I imposed was limiting the analysis to the parent subgroup (parent == 1). No other filters were applied. Because the codebook says every variable is observed for every participant, no complete-case restriction was needed.

commit_model: Linear regression model for each participant i: fin_security_avg_i = alpha + tau*treatment_i + sum_s gamma_s*1[site_i = s] (sites 2-4, site 1 as reference) + beta1*age_i + beta2*female_i + beta3*parent_i + sum_k delta_k*1[education_i = k] (categories 2, 3, 4; category 1 as reference) + beta4*household_size_i + beta5*employed_baseline_i + beta6*earnings_baseline_i + beta7*months_unemployed_baseline_i + e_i, with E[e_i | treatment, site, covariates] = 0. The model is linear and additive in these terms, and the treatment coefficient is the same for all participants and sites (no treatment-by-site or treatment-by-covariate interactions). Treatment was randomly assigned within site, so tau is interpreted as the average intention-to-treat effect of assignment to the program on the outcome, conditional on site and the baseline covariates. Observations are independent across participants. No parametric distribution (for example, normality) is assumed for the errors. Error variances may differ across participants (heteroskedasticity allowed), and no population variance is treated as known or restricted. No population parameters are fixed at known values.
commit_null: H0: tau = 0, meaning the coefficient on treatment (the effect of program assignment on the two-wave average financial security index, adjusted for site and baseline covariates) is zero. The alternative is two-sided: tau ≠ 0.
commit_population: Adults seeking work or better jobs who enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four sites, with randomization at a 1:1 ratio within site between program assignment and a control group that could use existing public services.
commit_outcome: fin_security_avg = (fin_security_m6 + fin_security_m12) / 2: the participant's financial security index (0-20 scale, higher means more secure) averaged over the 6-month and 12-month follow-ups after random assignment.
commit_sample_restrictions: none. The analysis uses all participants in the supplied file, with no analyst-imposed subgroup, filter, or eligibility rule. The codebook states that every participant completed both follow-ups and every variable is observed, so no complete-case exclusion applied.

commit_model: Linear regression (linear probability) model for the binary 12-month employment indicator: E[employed_m12 | treatment, site] = alpha + beta*treatment + site fixed effects (indicators for sites 2, 3, 4 relative to site 1), estimated within the analyst-selected subgroup. The estimand beta is the site-adjusted average effect of random assignment to Pathways to Work (intent-to-treat) on the probability of being employed in the 12-month survey week, among participants unemployed 6+ months at baseline. Site indicators are the only conditioning variables (because randomization was within site); no baseline covariates are included in the selected model. Observations (participants) are assumed independent; errors are allowed to be heteroskedastic, with no restriction that error variances are equal or known. No distributional form is assumed for the outcome beyond its conditional mean being linear in treatment and site; no population parameters are treated as known or fixed.
commit_null: H0: beta = 0, i.e., the coefficient on treatment (the site-adjusted intent-to-treat effect of program assignment on 12-month employment probability in the subgroup) is zero; two-sided alternative beta ≠ 0.
commit_population: Adults enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at the four sites who had been unemployed for 6 or more months at random assignment (long-term unemployed).
commit_outcome: employed_m12: binary indicator (1 = employed in the survey week at the 12-month follow-up, 0 otherwise), used untransformed.
commit_sample_restrictions: Analyst-imposed subgroup restriction: only participants with months_unemployed_baseline >= 6 (which excludes everyone employed at baseline, since they are coded 0, and everyone unemployed 1–5 months). No other filters. No complete-case restriction was needed because the codebook says all variables are observed for every participant. The trial's own eligibility (enrolled adults at four sites, randomized 1:1 within site) is part of the supplied design, not a restriction I added.

commit_model: Linear regression model for participants aged 45 or older: health_m12_i = alpha + tau * treatment_i + sum_{s=2..4} gamma_s * 1[site_i = s] + e_i, with E[e_i | treatment_i, site_i] = 0. treatment is the randomly assigned program indicator (randomization within site, half to each arm per site); site indicators (sites 1–4, site 1 as reference) are the intrinsic conditioning variables reflecting within-site randomization. No baseline covariates are included. The estimand tau is the site-adjusted average effect of assignment to the program (intention-to-treat) on 12-month self-rated health in the age-45+ subgroup, under a common (site-invariant) additive treatment effect. Observations are assumed independent across participants. No distributional form is assumed for the errors (no normality), and error variances are not assumed equal: they may differ by treatment arm, site, or individual (heteroskedasticity allowed). No population parameters are treated as known or fixed.
commit_null: H0: tau = 0, i.e. the coefficient on treatment is zero (no average effect of program assignment on 12-month self-rated health among participants aged 45+, conditional on site). Two-sided alternative: tau ≠ 0.
commit_population: Adults seeking work or better jobs who enrolled in and were randomized in the Pathways to Work evaluation at its four sites, restricted to those aged 45 or older at random assignment.
commit_outcome: health_m12: self-rated health at the 12-month follow-up, 1 = poor to 5 = excellent, used untransformed as a numeric score in its original 1–5 units.
commit_sample_restrictions: Analyst-imposed subgroup: participants with age >= 45 at random assignment (age 45 included). No other filters were applied, and no complete-case restriction was needed because, per the design, all variables are observed for every participant. The study design's own eligibility (enrolled adults at the four sites, randomized within site) is separate from this restriction.

commit_model: Linear regression (linear probability) model for a binary outcome: E[employed_m12 | treatment, site, X] = alpha + tau*treatment + site fixed effects (indicators for sites 2, 3, 4, site 1 as reference) + linear terms in age, female, parent, household_size, employed_baseline, earnings_baseline (dollars), months_unemployed_baseline, plus indicator terms for education categories (2, 3, 4 vs. 1 = less than high school). Treatment is randomly assigned within site (randomization stratified by site, roughly 1:1). The estimand tau is the average effect of being assigned to the program (intent-to-treat) on the probability of being employed at the 12-month follow-up, conditional on site and the listed baseline covariates, assumed constant (additive) across covariate values. Errors have conditional mean zero and are independent across participants. Error variances are not assumed equal; heteroskedasticity is allowed, with no known or fixed variance values. No other distributional form is assumed for the outcome beyond its being binary (0/1). No population parameters are treated as known.
commit_null: H0: tau = 0, i.e., the coefficient on treatment is zero (program assignment has no effect on the 12-month employment probability, conditional on site and baseline covariates). The alternative is two-sided: tau ≠ 0.
commit_population: Adults enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at the four evaluation sites, each randomly assigned within site to the program or to a control group that could use existing public services.
commit_outcome: employed_m12: binary indicator (1 = employed in the survey week at the 12-month follow-up after random assignment, 0 = not employed), used untransformed on its 0/1 scale. The treatment effect is a difference in probability (percentage points).
commit_sample_restrictions: None. The full sample of all participants was used, with no subgroup, site, or other filter. The code drops rows with missing values in the outcome, treatment, site, or covariates (a complete-case rule), but the supplied data had no missing values, so this rule removed no rows.

commit_model: Linear regression model for a randomized trial with assignment stratified by site: employed_m12_i = alpha + beta*treatment_i + sum over sites 2-4 of gamma_s*1(site_i = s) + e_i, where treatment_i is the randomly assigned program indicator (1 = program, 0 = control) and site fixed effects (four sites) are the only conditioning variables, included because randomization was conducted within site. No baseline covariates are included. The estimand beta is the site-adjusted average effect of assignment to the program (intent-to-treat) on the probability of being employed in the 12-month survey week, i.e., a difference in employment proportions (linear probability model). The error e_i has conditional mean zero given treatment and site. No distributional form is assumed for the outcome beyond this, and error variances may differ across observations (heteroskedasticity allowed, no homoskedasticity restriction, no known variance). Participants are treated as independent observations; there is no clustering or other dependence beyond the site stratification. No population parameters are fixed at known values.
commit_null: H0: beta = 0, meaning assignment to Pathways to Work has no site-adjusted average effect on the 12-month employment probability. The alternative is two-sided: beta != 0.
commit_population: Adults enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four sites, randomized within site to the program or to a control group with access to existing public services.
commit_outcome: employed_m12: a binary indicator equal to 1 if the participant was employed in the survey week 12 months after random assignment, used untransformed.
commit_sample_restrictions: none. The full randomized sample is used, with no subgroup, filter or eligibility rule added by the analyst. Only the design's own eligibility (enrollment in the trial) applies; the codebook says all variables are fully observed, so there was no complete-case restriction.

commit_model: A linear probability model for each participant i: employed_m12_i = alpha + beta * treatment_i + gamma_2 * 1[site_i = 2] + gamma_3 * 1[site_i = 3] + gamma_4 * 1[site_i = 4] + e_i, with E[e_i | treatment_i, site_i] = 0. Site 1 is the reference category. The site indicators are the only conditioning variables; no baseline covariates are included. Treatment is randomly assigned within site, so beta is the intention-to-treat effect of being assigned to Pathways to Work, as opposed to the existing public services available to controls, on the probability of being employed in the survey week 12 months after random assignment. Because the model has no treatment-by-site interactions, beta is a single common effect across sites; if effects differ by site, beta is a variance-weighted average of the within-site effects. Observations are independent across participants. The model assumes no distribution for the errors beyond that implied by a binary outcome: no normality, and error variances are unrestricted, so heteroskedasticity across participants is allowed, including by treatment arm and site. No population parameters, such as variances, are treated as known or fixed at particular values.
commit_null: H0: beta = 0, meaning assignment to the program has no effect on the conditional probability of employment at 12 months, holding site fixed. The alternative is two-sided: beta ≠ 0.
commit_population: Adults seeking work or better jobs who enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four sites and were randomly assigned, within site, to the program or to a control group.
commit_outcome: employed_m12: a binary indicator equal to 1 if the participant was employed in the survey week 12 months after random assignment, and 0 otherwise. It is used untransformed, on the probability scale.
commit_sample_restrictions: No subgroup, eligibility filter, or trimming was applied; all participants are included regardless of site, demographics, or baseline status. The only analyst-imposed rule is a complete-case restriction: rows missing employed_m12, treatment, or site are dropped. In the supplied data no values are missing, so no rows were removed.

commit_model: Linear regression (linear probability model) for a binary outcome: E[employed_m12 | X] = a + b*treatment + site fixed effects (indicators for sites 2–4, with site 1 as reference) + linear terms in age, female, parent, household_size, employed_baseline, earnings_baseline and months_unemployed_baseline + indicators for education categories 2, 3 and 4 (category 1 as reference). The conditional mean is assumed to be linear and additive in these terms, with no treatment-by-covariate or treatment-by-site interactions, so there is a single common treatment coefficient. Treatment is randomly assigned within site (1:1). Observations are independent across participants. Errors have mean zero given the regressors and may be heteroskedastic with unrestricted variances. No error distribution is assumed beyond this; no population variance or other parameter is treated as known or fixed. Estimand: b, the covariate- and site-adjusted intention-to-treat effect of being assigned to Pathways to Work on the probability of being employed at 12 months.
commit_null: H0: b = 0, i.e. the coefficient on treatment is zero (no effect of program assignment on the 12-month employment probability). Two-sided alternative: b ≠ 0.
commit_population: Adults seeking work or better jobs who enrolled in the Pathways to Work randomized evaluation at its four sites and were randomly assigned within site to the program or to the control group.
commit_outcome: employed_m12: a 0/1 indicator equal to 1 if the participant was employed in the survey week at the 12-month follow-up after random assignment. It is used untransformed.
commit_sample_restrictions: none — all randomized participants were used, with no subgroup, site, outlier or complete-case restriction.

commit_model: Linear regression model for participant i: health_m12_i = a + b1*treatment_i + b2*(age_i/10) + b3*treatment_i*(age_i/10) + site fixed effects (indicators for sites 2, 3, 4, with site 1 as reference) + e_i, with E[e_i | treatment_i, age_i, site_i] = 0. Treatment is randomly assigned within site. The conditional mean of the outcome is assumed linear in age, with a treatment effect that changes linearly in age. Site indicators are the intrinsic conditioning variables because randomization was within site; age (divided by 10) enters as both a main effect and a moderator of treatment. No other baseline covariates are in the model. Observations are assumed independent across participants. No distribution is assumed for the errors (no normality assumed), and error variances may differ across participants (heteroskedasticity allowed; no homoskedasticity restriction).
